sentences.sentence: The study aims to examine whether prospective teachers' use of digital video recordings (DVRs) affects their Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK).
It asks what impact DVR use has on TPACK and its seven domains, and why DVR use affects them.
A mixed methods approach combining a survey, interviews and classroom observation was used.

The quantitative strand was a quasi-experimental pre/post/delayed post design with an experimental and a control group of 35 prospective teachers each (70 in total) at Al-Qasmi Academic College of Education.
A self-report TPACK questionnaire was used, analysed with Quade's test and paired t-tests.
Ten experimental-group participants were interviewed in semi-structured interviews, analysed thematically.
The TPACK framework served as the study's conceptual framework and as an organizer of teacher knowledge.
Post-survey adjusted means were higher in the experimental group than in the control group.
Quade's test showed significant differences between the groups in all seven TPACK domains (overall F = 36.231, p = 0.001).
Paired t-tests showed significant improvement in the experimental group (overall t = 6.876, p = 0.001, d = 1.162) but not the control group (overall t = −0.265, p = 0.396).
Interviewees described using DVRs to identify and correct problems in each TPACK domain.
The authors state that DVR use had a significant impact on TPACK and attribute this to guided reflection and peer dialogue.
They recommend DVR use by all teachers, especially with group discussion, and recommend adopting the TPACK model to guide teacher education.
They note two limitations: groups were formed from different specializations, and the questionnaire responses are self-reported, which should be taken into account when generalizing.

introduction: this study aims to examine whether the use of DVRs by prospective teachers affects their Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK).
What is the impact of prospective teachers’ use of DVRs on their Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) and its seven domains: (TK, PK, CK, PCK, TCK, TPK, TPACK)?
How does the use of DVRs affect Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) and its seven domains: (TK, PK, CK, PCK, TCK, TPK, TPACK)?
methodology: The study employed a mixed methods approach, combining both quantitative and qualitative methods
the researcher adopted a quasi-experimental design, utilizing a pre-survey and post-survey design with two groups: experimental and control.
The study involved a sample of 70 prospective teachers at Al-Qasmi Academic College of Education.
The number of prospective teachers in each of the experimental and control groups was 35 prospective teachers.
The present research utilized a self-report questionnaire for the TPACK domains and subdomains before and after the experiment
semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 prospective teachers from the experimental group.

results: Generally, the experimental group had higher mean scores in the TPACK components than the control group.
Table 5 shows that the differences in the mean scores of TPACK domains, and between the experimental and control groups, are significant.

The participating prospective teachers reported that using DVRs had a significant positive impact on the development of TPACK.
discussion: The study demonstrated that using DVRs as a professional development tool for prospective teachers had a significant impact on their TPACK, perceptions, and experiences.
This positive impact is attributed to guided reflection and peer dialogue in helping teachers connect theory to practice
the use of DVRs by prospective and in-service teachers is recommended, especially when the teachers collaborate and discuss the DVRs in a group.
We recommend the adoption of the TPACK model to guide the education of prospective teachers
The experimental and control groups were formed from different specializations as each specialization included a small number of prospective teachers.
The generalization of the results should take into account the fact that the responses are self-reported.
